whatItIs.heading: What is water damage clean-up?
whatItIs.body: Water damage clean-up is the systematic removal and sanitization phase that follows initial water extraction. Once standing water has been extracted, a structure is left with saturated materials, potential contamination, and conditions that will develop mold within 24 to 48 hours if left unaddressed. Clean-up covers the controlled demolition of materials that cannot be dried in place—soaked drywall, saturated insulation, buckled flooring—antimicrobial treatment of structural surfaces, containment to prevent contamination from spreading to unaffected areas, and the clearing and documentation of all debris for insurance purposes. It is not the same as extraction alone, and it is not the same as the reconstruction phase that follows. Clean-up is the bridge between stopping the event and repairing the structure.

process.heading: How Gallagher handles water damage clean-up

steps.title: Contamination classification and containment
steps.body: The crew assesses whether the water event involved Category 1 (clean), Category 2 (gray), or Category 3 (black water) contamination. Containment barriers—plastic sheeting, negative air pressure—are installed before any demolition begins to prevent cross-contamination into unaffected rooms.

steps.title: Controlled removal of unsalvageable materials
steps.body: Saturated drywall, insulation, flooring, and cabinetry that cannot be dried in place are removed in a controlled sequence. All debris is catalogued and bagged per contamination category. Documentation is prepared in parallel for the insurance adjuster.

steps.title: Antimicrobial treatment of structural surfaces
steps.body: Exposed framing, subfloor, and concrete are treated with EPA-registered antimicrobial agents to halt mold colonization. In Category 2 and 3 events, this step is non-negotiable—skipping it converts a clean-up job into a mold remediation job within days.

steps.title: Clearance documentation and handoff to drying or repair
steps.body: Before the clean-up phase closes, moisture readings confirm that all remaining structural materials are within acceptable drying range. The structure is documented and ready for either continued structural drying or the reconstruction phase—handled by the same Gallagher crew.

signs.heading: Signs you need water damage clean-up now

items.title: Water has been extracted but the structure still smells
items.body: A persistent damp or sour odor after extraction means contaminated residue, mold spores, or wet material remains inside walls or under flooring. Extraction alone does not clean a water-damaged structure.

items.title: Drywall is soft, crumbling, or showing visible staining
items.body: Drywall that has been wet for more than a few hours typically cannot be dried in place without trapping moisture inside. It needs to be removed before mold establishes behind the surface.

items.title: Flooring is delaminating, cupping, or separating
items.body: Buckled hardwood, lifted tile, and delaminating laminate all indicate the subfloor below is wet. The surface material generally cannot be saved and needs to be removed to access and dry the structural layer beneath.

items.title: The water source was gray or black water
items.body: Gray water from appliances or drains and black water from sewage or outdoor flooding require antimicrobial treatment of every surface the water contacted. Standard cleaning products are not sufficient.

items.title: Visible mold is already present
items.body: If mold is visible on any surface within the affected area, clean-up must include mold containment protocols. Proceed to mold remediation in parallel—do not attempt to clean mold with bleach and move on.

pricing.heading: Water damage clean-up pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Every job starts with a free on-site assessment. Water damage clean-up in Southern California typically runs $1,000–$7,500. The low end covers a contained single-room event with clean water, limited material removal, and straightforward antimicrobial treatment. The upper end reflects multi-room events involving Category 2 or 3 contamination, significant controlled demolition, and extensive documentation requirements for the insurance claim. Square footage of affected area, contamination category, and the volume of materials requiring removal are the primary cost drivers. Reconstruction costs—replacing what was removed—are separate and are quoted after the clean-up phase is complete and moisture clearance is confirmed. Gallagher Restoration Co. coordinates directly with your insurance carrier and documents everything needed for the adjuster from day one.

faqs.q: What is the difference between water damage clean-up and water extraction?
faqs.a: Water extraction removes standing liquid. Water damage clean-up addresses everything that follows: removing saturated materials that cannot be saved, treating structural surfaces with antimicrobials to prevent mold, containing contamination, and preparing the structure for drying and repair. Extraction is the first 30 minutes; clean-up is the next several days.

faqs.q: Can I do water damage clean-up myself?
faqs.a: For small, clean-water events in non-porous areas—a minor sink overflow on sealed tile, for example—homeowner cleanup is possible. For any event involving carpet, drywall, insulation, subfloor, or gray or black water, professional clean-up is strongly recommended. The risk is hidden moisture that triggers mold and voids insurance coverage for secondary damage.

faqs.q: How quickly does mold start after water damage in Southern California?
faqs.a: Mold can begin colonizing within 24 to 48 hours in warm, humid interior conditions—faster in summer months in the Inland Empire and low-desert areas. Southern California's climate accelerates the timeline compared to cooler regions. Clean-up needs to begin within the first day to prevent mold from becoming a separate remediation project.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover water damage clean-up costs?
faqs.a: Most standard California homeowners policies cover water damage clean-up when the source was sudden and accidental—a burst pipe, appliance failure, or storm event. Gallagher Restoration Co. builds the documentation package from day one—categorizing the event, itemizing removed materials, and photographing every phase—so the adjuster has what is needed to process the claim.
